newsitem.title: USA: CBOT's Arbor says more Dow index products in works.
newsitem.headline: CBOT's Arbor says more Dow index products in works.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade Chairman Patrick Arbor said Thursday the exchange plans to introduce additional futures and options products based on Dow indexes within the next two years.

The licensing pact signed earlier this month with Dow Jones & Co. gives CBOT the right to list products on all Dow indexes except the Taiwan stock index, which trades at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, Arbor told members attending a midyear chairman's briefing.

Following a planned October launch for futures and futures-options on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the CBOT plans within two years to roll out products based on the Dow utilities, transportation and composite indexes as well as several of Dow's global indexes, Arbor said.
"The Dow accord will actually bring a wealth of products to the members of the Chicago Board of Trade," he said.
He added the exchange was currently in talks with Dow Jones regarding opportunities in the area of technology and quote distribution.

In response to a member's question, Arbor said Dow Jones did not grant the CBOT the right to offer Dow products on Project A, the exchange's after-hours electronic system. While the exchange "left the door open" in hopes of extending its trading hours for the Dow products, Arbor said, it was his understanding the company was looking to license Dow indexes in other money-center time zones.

The addition of the Dow contracts also means the exchange will re-examine a recent decision not to lengthen the trading day for Treasury contracts because the exchange wants to encourage synergies to develop between bonds and equities, Arbor said.
"We're going to take another hard look at that again," he said.
CBOT directors in May voted to rescind a previous decision to extend trading hours for the financial session, which currently ends at 1400 CDT. DJIA futures and options will trade until 1515 CDT.

At this afternoon's address to members, Arbor also unveiled plans to construct two new trading pits that will house DJIA futures and options, plus about 100 new booths to service order flow. The DJIA futures pit will span 1,250 square feet.
